subtitle: After 50+ lessons of frameworks and rules, you face the final task: turn this knowledge into YOUR system. A written rulebook covering setup criteria, sizing, execution, and review — refined by YOUR data. This is what separates traders who actually do it from those who just keep reading.

blocks.content:
You've now learned position sizing, risk management, chart reading, indicators, advanced concepts, macro context, and execution discipline. That's a lot of knowledge. But knowledge alone doesn't make traders profitable — APPLIED knowledge does.

This penultimate lesson is about CONSTRUCTION: assembling everything into your own personalized trading system. A written rulebook that codifies what you'll trade, how you'll size it, what state you'll trade in, and how you'll improve over time.
Why you NEED a written system

blocks.title: Unwritten rules are no rules
blocks.content:
Most retail traders have 'rules' that exist only in their head. The problem: when emotion is high (during drawdowns, FOMO moments, tilt), the mental rules become very negotiable. 'I usually risk 1%, but this trade is special, so I'll go 5%.' The unwritten rule fails exactly when it's needed.

A WRITTEN system makes rules concrete. They become public commitments to yourself. Breaking written rules is visible and uncomfortable in a way that breaking mental rules isn't. The friction of going against your written system is itself the discipline mechanism.

rows: Specific patterns you trade + required confluences
Risk % per trade, leverage rules, sizing math
Order types, SL placement, TP strategy, OCO usage
Pre-session readiness, Trade Apgar, hard daily stop
How you'll update the system based on data

blocks.content:
Define SPECIFIC setups you'll trade. Not 'I'll trade when it looks good'. Specific like:

  • Setup A — Wyckoff Spring Long: at confirmed accumulation range support, wick below + close back above + 2× average volume on wick.
  • Setup B — HTF Pullback Long: 1D uptrend, 4H pullback to 50 EMA + horizontal support, bullish engulfing + above-avg volume + RSI bullish divergence.
  • Setup C — Bearish Engulfing Short: at major resistance after sustained uptrend, bearish engulfing + 2× volume + RSI bearish divergence.

3-5 specific setups is enough. Anything that doesn't match one of your defined setups = not a trade. This is the single biggest filter to your edge.

From lessons 6 and 7:

  • Risk per trade: 1% standard, 2% on rare A+ setups (Apgar 9-10).
  • Sizing formula: notional = ($risk) / (SL distance %).
  • Leverage: isolated margin always (unless specific hedging exception). Maximum leverage 10×. Match leverage to SL distance, not feeling.
  • Daily drawdown stop: at -3% from session open, stop all trading. At -5% from peak equity, drop to small-size or paper for re-validation.
  • Total exposure cap: maximum X open positions simultaneously (e.g., 3-5) to avoid concentration risk.

From lessons 3 and 5:

  • Default order type: limit. Market only for forced exits or known-thin breakouts.
  • SL placement: structural (below swing low/OB/FVG zone) + ATR buffer (~1.5× ATR minimum). Always use reduce-only flag on stop losses.
  • TP strategy: OCO pair immediately after entry. TP1 at first major resistance (partial close 50%); TP2 at next major level (partial); runner with trailing stop.
  • Funding awareness: don't long during extreme positive funding (+0.08%+ per 8h) without specific contrarian setup. Check funding before sizing.

From lessons 9, 46, 47:

  • Pre-session readiness check: 4 dimensions (sleep/mood/P&L/preparation). Any RED = no trading.
  • Trade Apgar score: ≥7 total AND no zeros required to take any trade.
  • No trades for 30 min after any loss; 24h after any 2× normal loss.
  • Hard daily stop at -3%: close platform, walk away.
  • Pre-planned setups only: trade ideas defined BEFORE the session, not during it.

From lessons 48, 49:

  • Daily (5 min): review today's trades, note deviations from plan, one action item for tomorrow.
  • Weekly (30 min): aggregate stats, identify ONE strength + ONE weakness, action for next week.
  • Monthly (1-2h): setup-type performance, behavioral patterns, ONE specific improvement project for next month.
  • Quarterly (half-day): strategy-level review, market regime check, scale up/down/maintain decision.

Your system isn't static. As you gather data:

  • Add proven setups: if a specific setup shows positive R-multiple over 30+ trades, codify it.
  • Remove failing setups: if a specific setup shows negative R-multiple over 30+ trades, stop trading it.
  • Adjust thresholds: if your 7-Apgar trades are losing but 8+ are winning, raise the threshold.
  • Refine criteria: discover specific conditions where a setup works vs fails, add those filters.
  • Periodically prune: complexity creep is real. Every 3-6 months, ask 'what rules am I no longer using? Why?' Remove dead weight.

The system evolves with you and the market. The discipline is updating it BASED ON DATA, not on feelings or recent results.

Your written system can be 1-3 pages total. Example outline:

MY TRADING SYSTEM v1.0

1. SETUPS I TRADE:
   - Wyckoff Spring Long (at accumulation range)
   - HTF Pullback Long (1D up + 4H 50EMA pullback + engulfing + vol + RSI div)
   - Bearish Engulfing Short (at HTF resistance + vol + RSI bearish div)
   - SMC Liquidity Sweep (LTF hunt + OB return + reversal candle)

2. SIZING: 1% risk per trade (2% on Apgar 9-10 only). Isolated margin. Max 10x leverage.

3. EXECUTION: Limit orders default. SL = structural + 1.5x ATR. OCO with TP1/TP2 immediately. Funding check before sizing.

4. STATE: Pre-session 4-dim check. Apgar >=7 no zeros. No trades 30min after loss. -3% daily stop.

5. REVIEW: Daily 5min, Weekly 30min, Monthly 1-2h, Quarterly half-day.

6. EVOLUTION: Track per-setup R-multiple over 30+ trades. Add/remove setups based on data. Re-evaluate quarterly.

blocks.title: Take this with you
blocks.content:
Three rules:

  1. Write your system down. Unwritten rules fail when emotion is high.
  2. Keep it simple. 1-3 pages, 6 sections. Don't over-engineer.
  3. Evolve based on data, not feelings. Every 3-6 months, update what works/fails based on actual R-multiple data.
